newsitem.title: MEXICO: Alestra says to invest $70 mln '96 in Guadalajara.
newsitem.headline: Alestra says to invest $70 mln '96 in Guadalajara.

text.p: Telecommunications operator Alestra will close 1996 with a $70 million investment in infrastructure in Guadalajara, regional director Diana Sanchez said.
"Here in Guadalajara, by year's end we'll have $70 million...(invested) in infrastructure, in fiber optics, central offices and all necessary equipment," Sanchez said.

Alestra is a joint venture between U.S. based AT&T Corp and Mexican conglomerate Alfa, among others, to provide long-distance telephone services after the market in Mexico is open to competition on January 1, 1997.
Guadalajara is Mexico's second city, from where Alestra plans to cover nine of Mexico's 32 states.
Sanchez said that Alestra planned to increase its payroll from 250 employees in August to 500 by year-end and 1,000 next year.
